build: OUG disk crack, both trainers declined

extra: Expanded LEVELD stream through the final output pointer at $0A/$0B

comments.text: LEVELD sprite slots for VIC pointers $80–$8F in bank $4000. Each slot has 63 pixel bytes followed by a byte outside the VIC's sprite fetch.
The byte at $6001 belongs to the first sprite's 63-byte pattern. The stage loader uses this address for the length high byte before overwriting it with expanded sprite data.

Translate each of LEVELD's 256 character indices to a colour byte for the viewport renderer at $131B.
The first 128 glyphs for LEVELD. The IRQ at $0C84 selects the 2 KB character set with $D018 = $0E while VIC bank $4000 is selected.
The low page of the playfield character set continues here, starting at glyph $1B. The VIC reads eight pattern bytes per glyph.
LEVELD supplies initial eight-byte patterns for glyphs $2C through $2F. The frame-copy loop writes 32 bytes to this range at $C64C.
Eight-byte glyph patterns for indices $30 through $7F. The VIC fetches them from the playfield character set at $7800 when those character codes appear on screen.
LEVELD's glyphs $80-$FF continue the character set at $7800. Each glyph occupies eight bytes.

Two background colour values passed from the LEVELD header through $E374/$E375 to VIC registers $D022/$D023.
Copied to $E375 by $156D, then written to $D023 by the raster handler.
Remaining header bytes before the tile-patch pointer. The loader's stage-zero decision reads byte $C00A at $32DB.
The loader compares the requested stage against this byte at $32DB on its zero-index branch. LEVELD supplies three.
Pointer to the table of two-byte tile patch addresses read by $37B1 and $37B6.
High byte used by $37A7 when taking the address of the pointer table.
Setup copies $C00D into $6F at $1573. The purpose of the adjacent header byte is open.
The resident candidate-position routine at $1D40 reads seventeen here as the threshold for $1ACA.
The resident loop at $0965 reads this word and dispatches to $C298 through $15EB.
High byte of the update callback loaded at $096A.
Holds 20 ten-byte descriptors selected by the resident routine at $1965. The last two bytes of each record are the routine address read at $1DC9 and $1DCE.
Holds 103 object records. Setup at $3765 reads column, row, type and flags. The row and column choose where the tile patch begins when flag $20 is set.
The first $FF in the column field ends LEVELD's object list at $3773. The final record is four bytes of $FF.
Initialize the viewport row to $AB in $46 and its column to $00 in $45. Store the row plus $0A in $E690 and the column plus $0F in $E630. Clear $1D, $1F and $390C and return with carry set.
Return immediately from the actor callback. The corresponding descriptor slot passes control through $15EB and this RTS returns to the engine.
Forward the resident engine's stage update callback to $C629.
The 12 pointers index LEVELD's rectangular tile patches. $37B1 reads the low byte and $37B6 reads the next byte for the high byte.
A 2-column by 1-row tile patch, entry 0 in LEVELD's pointer table. The two dimensions precede 2 character bytes copied to the map by $37D5.

Set extents to ten and nineteen, set $E9F0 and $EA80 to two, and set horizontal movement to eight. Enable direct shape selection and set colour twelve.
Initialize LEVELD actor type $25 in slot X. Clear visibility flag $40.
Set $EA50 to $FF and, if the low three actor flag bits are nonzero, copy them to $E840 and clear them in the flags byte.
Supply horizontal extent two and vertical extent three before transferring actor flags at $C35C.
Supply three as the horizontal extent by jumping into the store at $C376. The rest of that path sets vertical extent three and transfers the flag bits.
A standalone return separates the flag-capture initializers from $C387.

Initialize LEVELD actor type $2E in slot X. Store $01 in horizontal extent, vertical extent. Apply $34 with OR to actor flags. Apply $01 with OR to shape and actor flags at $EB10. Store $FF in $EA50. Store $0F in $E870.
Preserve the existing actor flags and set bit $20 in the slot indexed by X.
Initialize LEVELD actor type $34 in slot X. Store $02 in horizontal extent, vertical extent. Store $FF in $EA50.

Initialize LEVELD actor type $2C in slot X. Store $12 in vertical extent. Store $0A in horizontal extent. Store $02 in $E9F0, sprite colour. Store $04 in $EA80. Enable direct sprite shape selection by setting bit $80 at $EB10.
Initialize LEVELD actor type $32 in slot X. Store $13 in vertical extent. Store $0A in horizontal extent. Store $02 in $E9F0. Store $04 in $EA80. Store $0E in sprite colour.
Finish with extents ten and eighteen, $E9F0 and $EA80 both three, colour eight, flag $04 set and $E870 equal to $0F.
Initialize LEVELD actor type $36 in slot X. Store $04 in sprite colour. Store $00 in $E870.

Initialize LEVELD actor type $35 in slot X. Store $0A in horizontal extent. Store $12 in vertical extent. Store $03 in $E9F0, $EA80. Enable direct sprite shape selection by setting bit $80 at $EB10. Store $02 in sprite colour. Apply $04 with OR to actor flags. Store $0F in $E870.

Set movement five, extents $24 and $3F, $E9F0 to six and $EA80 to zero. Clear $1D, $1F and $E9C0, then apply $C4D5. Allocate types $27 through $2B and give each the parent's coordinates and parent slot.

Initialize LEVELD actor types $27, $28, $29, $2A, $2B in slot X. Enable direct sprite shape selection by setting bit $80 at $EB10. Store $0E in sprite colour. Store $FF in $EA50. Apply $10 with OR to actor flags.
Set $EA50 to $FF, $E9F0 and $EA80 to four and six, and extents to eight and eleven. Hide the actor through $C353.
A standalone return immediately before the type $25 replacement callback.
When $1D is nonzero, keep its low seven bits at $70, set $1E to three and allocate type $25 at the old actor's position. Mark the old actor for removal, pass the new slot to $3854 and set $4F to $FF.

Set movement to $10. After $275A returns carry clear, require $E840 zero, a successful $2760 check with ten and zero in the low six random bits before requesting type $2E through $28AF. Finish at the turn routine with four in $08.

Choose shape zero or two from the direction bit and call $2742 and $275A. On carry clear, call $2838 when $E840 equals $E870 and count $E840 down. At zero apply the turn logic and set horizontal movement to $10.

On carry from $22E5 advance one coarse row and call $381A. Remove the actor if $E840 is zero. Otherwise add $1A to the field for the new type, call $3854 and clear the removal flag. Then test proximity with $279E and $2760 and pass a parameter chosen by relative coarse X to $27DA.
An extra return lies between the converting actor and the hidden trigger update.
When $1F is set increment sprite colour and set visibility. Check each active player unless $1D is negative. Carry from $23D6 calls $216F and removes the actor.
Decrement $E870. A negative result flags the actor for removal. Otherwise continue to $287A.
Call the resident contact check when the tile animation phase is zero.

Decrement the timer at $C6B8. When it underflows, reload $0A and advance the phase at $C6B9 modulo four. Copy 32 bytes backwards into $7960–$797F, replacing glyphs $2C–$2F in the playfield character set.
The four phase offsets $1F, $3F, $5F and $3F point to the last byte of each 32-byte animation frame relative to $C658. The copying loop counts down from the selected end.
Four consecutive eight-byte glyph bitmaps for animation phase 0. This frame replaces playfield glyphs $2C–$2F.
Four consecutive eight-byte glyph bitmaps for animation phase 1 and 3. This frame replaces playfield glyphs $2C–$2F.
Four consecutive eight-byte glyph bitmaps for animation phase 2. This frame replaces playfield glyphs $2C–$2F.
Countdown in calls to the stage update. Underflow reloads it with $0A and advances the animation phase.
The update increments this value modulo four and uses it to index the backwards-copy offsets at $C654.
Select direct shape $C9 or $CA from the direction flag and continue through the moving update at $C534.
Decrement $E750 and reset it to three on underflow. Combine the toggled low shape bit with the pair selected by the direction flag. Finish at $C534.
Call $2757 with six and decrement $E870. A negative result reloads it with $28 and attempts to spawn type $2E.
Jump to the shared patrol update at $C534.

When $E750 reaches zero reload it to two and increment the four-state phase. Derive the shape group from signed vertical movement, or from the direction of nonzero horizontal movement when vertical movement is zero. OR it with the phase to index $C753 and then run $C534.
Four groups of four sprite pointers for negative vertical, positive vertical and the two horizontal directions.
Call $279E with two, and on carry set call $2760 with five for the final proximity result.
On a successful proximity test spawn three type $32 actors with the records from $C816, then flag the parent for removal through $C7B4.
On carry from $C763 supply type $33 and continue to the offset-table spawn routine.
On a successful proximity test spawn four type $32 actors from the records at $C825 and then remove their parent.
On a successful proximity test spawn four type $32 actors from the records at $C839 and then remove their parent.
Pass the type, count and record pointer through to $C7BB, then flag the original actor for removal.

Take child type from A and count from Y. Allocate each child, add the first two record bytes to the parent's coarse coordinates, copy byte two into $E840 and $E870, and use the last two bytes as movement. Advance the pointer by five and restore X after each child.
Scratch byte where $C7BB keeps the requested child type for its successive allocations.

Twelve five-byte offset records. The spawn branches read batches of three, four and four from $C816, $C825 and $C839 respectively. The final additional record at $C84D shares the layout of coarse offsets, a shared timer value and two movement values.
On a successful proximity test use the three records at $C816 to spawn type $33 and remove the source.

Run $275A and set colour eight. Select a default direct shape from $BF or $C1 using the flags, then allow the movement comparison to select $C0 or $C2. Store the shape and call the turn logic with A equal to four.

Set $E9C0 to four unless $E960 is five, in which case set it to two. On the first path optionally spawn type $2E according to random bit $10. Reload a negative $E750 with ten and call $1B75 with four.

Call $38BD and, while $390C is clear, choose colour fourteen or three by $23B7. Carry from $275A sets $390C to $14, restores actor type $26 and clears visibility. Other paths update the parent's shape and toggle direction on $E9C0 underflow.
Select a shape from $CA6E using the parent phase and copy the parent position with three added to coarse X.
Select a shape from $CA7E and copy the parent's position with $0280 added to the two-byte Y coordinate. Random values below three request type $2E through $28AF.
Select a shape from $CA8E and follow the parent at coarse X plus three and two-byte Y plus $0280. Random values below $1E cause a type $2E allocation.
Select a shape from $CA9E and copy the parent's position, applying ADC with five to coarse Y. This entry leaves the incoming carry in the addition.
Select a shape from $CAAE, copy the parent position and add three to coarse X. The carry from that addition flows into the ADC of five on coarse Y.
Copy the parent colour. Remove the child if $390C is set, the parent's type differs from $26, or its flags are zero or have bit zero set.
Jump to the shared return immediately after the parent's type check.
Read the parent's flags. A zero byte or a set removal bit sends the child to $2739. Otherwise return to the actor loop.
Count $CABF down. On underflow reload it to six and advance the phase at $CABE modulo twelve. Load the selected shape from $CA5E and store it at $E7E0.
Sprite pointer sequence used by the type $26 update. The phase counter at $CABE wraps at twelve.
Type $27 uses the shared phase at $CABE to select a pointer here for the child at coarse X plus three.
Type $28 selects its shape from this sequence before adding $0280 to the parent's Y coordinate.
Type $29 uses this sequence for the child offset on both axes.
Sprite pointers selected by type $2A for the child whose update applies ADC to coarse Y only.
Sprite pointers selected by type $2B, whose position update applies additions to both coarse axes.
Shared shape selector for the main actor and its five linked children. The update at $CA3D wraps it from eleven to zero.
Countdown reset to six by $CA3D before incrementing the shared shape phase.
